item1_same_input.route: independent pandas mirror written from the Pine T1 spec (not a literal swap of another family's mirror), engine and mirror on identical DB bars
item1_same_input.sufficiency_predicate: raw_T1 -> bc in {T4, T6, T1G, T2G, T1} — T1 is fifth in the bull priority order, so exactly four codes may absorb it; anything else is a violation

prev_doji_census_DESCRIPTIVE.role: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. T1 can mechanically follow a previous doji, so unlike T3 there is no impossibility to prove and no zero gate is applied. Splitting prev-bear from prev-doji would be a NEW family and a NEW multiplicity decision, not part of V1.

configuration.doji_rule: isDoji = (close == open) — EXACT equality; the doji_thresh parameter exists in the signature but is not consumed on this path
configuration.engulf_rule: engOk = cBody/max(pBody, 1e-10) >= min_body_ratio AND cTop >= pTop AND pBot >= cBot, with use_wick=False so the extremes are body extremes — this is what T4/T6 need, and T4/T6 are two of the four codes that outrank T1
configuration.why_attached: T1's canonical membership depends on this configuration through the priority resolution, so the definition is not reproducible without it

cross_vintage.current_store_raw_vs_materialized: CROSS-VINTAGE DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — the sealed build vintage recorded overlap 219,016 / 220,351 = 99.39% with residual 1,335; a reconciliation figure, never a semantic PASS

restriction_effects.reading: two grammar classes with different full memberships can share one OVERLAP-RESTRICTED membership signature; the estimand counts the restricted signature, so such a pair collapses to one final claim. This is the estimand definition working, not a defect — it is reported as a count and carried in the identity below.

eligibility_uniformity.law: aliases share an exact membership_hash, hence identical overlap statistics, hence identical eligibility — removal is CLASS-WHOLE by construction

by_ast.reading: the eligibility function references only the two overlap counts and the registered floors

item3_retention.note: the sweep is not vacuous: the same table shows how many eligible claims a retention gate WOULD remove at each threshold, and the sealed eligible set is the ungated one
item3_retention.provenance: an unregistered inherited retention gate was identified during pre-first-use review and removed before the first estimand execution; retention has been a stored diagnostic ever since

item4_clock.explicit: computed for T1 in this module — not inherited from another family's gate

item5_determinism.note: run2 consumes a row-shuffled source under a NEW seed (811), so the equality is both a rerun proof and an order-independence proof
